description:
Project: “Perf baseline & representative workload suite” (Serving Runtime Performance: kernel + scheduling). Redwood Inference will establish a durable set of Q1 2026 latency/throughput baselines across the top production model families and traffic shapes, and operationalize those baselines as regression gates for runtime releases.

Goals:
- Define “representative workloads” that match real production traffic (prompt length distributions, prefill/decode mix, streaming vs non-streaming, concurrency, batchability, caching hit-rates).
- Produce a Q1 2026 baseline report for top models on supported GPU SKUs/regions, with clear metric definitions (TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, throughput, tail behavior) and run conditions.
- Integrate the workload suite into automated canaries/CI so kernel/scheduler changes are evaluated consistently, with agreed-upon thresholds and triage workflows.
- Improve measurement correctness and repeatability (clock sync, warmup, isolation, kernel selection determinism, tracing/metrics alignment) so results are trusted by Runtime, SRE, and Product.

Scope:
- In scope: runtime scheduler (continuous batching, queueing, backpressure/load shedding), kernel selection stability, benchmark harness and runner infra, telemetry and dashboards for perf results, and release gating policy.
- Out of scope: model quality evals (owned by Applied ML/Evals), major customer-facing pricing/packaging changes, and new hardware bring-up beyond documenting experimental runs.

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Executive/engineering sponsor: Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng, Runtime); oversight: Ava Chen (CTO).
- Primary engineering owners: Sofia Ivanova (EM, Runtime Scheduling), Hiro Tanaka (EM, Runtime Kernels), Noah Patel (Sr Staff, Runtime).
- Benchmarking methodology and workload representativeness: Jonas Weber (Dir Perf & Evals), Claire Dubois (Sr Research Eng), Rina Kobayashi (Perf Benchmarks).
- Reliability + regression governance: Neha Kapoor (VP Infra & Reliability), Sean Gallagher (Dir SRE), Allison Grant (Observability).
- Telemetry pipelines/dashboards: Logan Wright (EM Telemetry), Nadia Rahman / Caleb Johnson.
- Release operationalization: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng Lead), Sahana Iyer (CI/Build).
- Product consumers of results (for transparency/positioning and internal roadmap): Nikhil Sharma / Henry Cho (Hosted API), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated).

Timeline (Q1 2026):
- Phase 0 (late Dec 2025–early Jan 2026): metric definitions + methodology ADRs; pick initial “top models” set and hardware matrix.
- Phase 1 (Jan 2026): implement/repair benchmark harness, runner isolation, and scheduler/kernel instrumentation; create first workload suite configs.
- Phase 2 (Feb 2026): run baseline across regions/SKUs; validate repeatability; build dashboards and automated comparison reports.
- Phase 3 (Mar 2026): publish baseline report internally; wire regression gates into perf-canary + release checklist; define triage and exception policy.

Constraints and deliverables:
- Constraints: noisy neighbors and fleet contention, GPU/driver variability, kernel auto-selection nondeterminism, metric drift between tracing vs client-side timers, and ensuring workloads remain representative as product features evolve (streaming, structured outputs, caching).
- Deliverables: (1) workload suite spec + configs, (2) benchmark methodology and runbook, (3) Q1 2026 baseline report and dashboards, (4) CI/perf-canary integration with thresholds + exception process, (5) recurring review cadence for updating baselines each quarter.

files.description: Published overview page: objectives, scope, owners, model list, hardware/region matrix, and links to dashboards, harness repo paths, and the Q1 baseline report.
Methodology doc defining metrics (TTFT/TPOT/e2e/p50/p95/p99), warmup rules, request generation, streaming measurement, and how to compare runs statistically.
Catalog of traffic shapes (short chat, long-context chat, batchable summarization, tool-calling bursts, mixed prompt distributions) with parameter ranges and rationale.
Spec for the workload suite format (YAML/JSON configs), versioning strategy, “top model” selection criteria, and rules for adding/updating workloads without breaking comparability.
Design note for scheduler instrumentation required for baselines: queue time, batch formation time, prefill/decode service time, cache hit/miss counters, and backpressure signals.
Step-by-step profiling playbook (nsys/nvprof equivalents, CPU flamegraphs, Triton/CUDA kernel traces) used to explain baseline results and regressions.
Dashboard spec (Grafana/Console internal) for baseline runs: breakdown views, run-to-run comparison, and annotations for runtime version/driver/kernel set.
ADR capturing final definitions for TTFT/TPOT and tail latency reporting, including streaming semantics and how client vs server timing is reconciled.
Engineering standard for perf regression gating: thresholds by workload, when to block merges/releases, exception workflow, and required evidence for overrides.
Top-level Linear initiative issue: “Perf baseline & representative workload suite (Q1 2026)” with milestones, sub-issues, and cross-team dependencies.
Implement benchmark runner isolation + determinism (pinned clocks, driver capture, kernel selection seed, warmup protocol) to reduce run variance.
Add workload configs for mixed prompt-length distributions and bursty concurrency; acceptance criteria includes reproducible p95/p99 under defined load.
Scheduler metrics instrumentation work item (queue time, batch size histograms, prefill/decode split) including exposure to telemetry pipeline.
Kernel microbenchmark suite alignment: ensure kernel-level metrics correlate with end-to-end baselines; define which kernels are ‘tracked’ per GPU SKU.
Perf-canary integration: nightly baseline runs, automatic diffing vs last good baseline, and Slack notifications + links to dashboards.
CI gating for runtime PRs touching scheduler/kernel paths: select representative subset of workloads and define pass/fail criteria and rerun policy.
Baseline report generation pipeline: turn raw run artifacts into a standardized report (tables, charts, confidence intervals) stored as versioned artifacts.
SRE + Runtime triage workflow: playbook for investigating regressions (who owns what, required logs, rollback criteria, and exception handling).
Q1 2026 baseline publication task: internal comms, review checklist, and sign-offs from Runtime, Evals, SRE, and Product.
PR: Add scheduler-level timing spans and counters required for baseline attribution (queue/batch/prefill/decode), including tests and metric naming conventions.
PR: Fix nondeterministic kernel selection under mixed sequence lengths (pin heuristics + logging of chosen kernels) to stabilize baseline runs.
PR: Implement backpressure/load-shedding hooks used by benchmark traffic generator to avoid invalid overload regimes and to record rejection behavior.
PR: Add structured ‘run manifest’ emitted by runtime (model hash, quant profile, driver, build id, flags) consumed by baseline report pipeline.
PR: Runtime metrics cardinality reduction + new histogram buckets for TTFT/TPOT to support dashboard comparisons without blowing up telemetry.
PR: Scheduler change to improve tail latency under bursty traffic (batch formation cap + fairness tweak), including before/after benchmark evidence.
PR: Add benchmark-mode config flag to disable non-essential features (debug logging, extra tracing) and document the impact on latency measurement.
PR: Add regression test that runs a small representative workload in CI with fixed seed and validates TTFT/TPOT within tolerance bands.
PR: Add workload suite schema + validation, and new traffic-shape definitions for long-context and mixed prompt distributions.
PR: Improve runner repeatability (warmup stage, CPU affinity pinning, GPU clock settings) and emit richer artifacts for report generation.
PR: Nightly baseline workflow: schedule, environment reservation, artifact upload, and automatic diff comment posted into Slack channels.
PR: Add ‘baseline gate’ step used by release branches; includes override mechanism with required justification fields.
PR: Add dashboards/alerts templates for baseline regression detection (TTFT/TPOT deltas, confidence bands, run variance alarms).
PR: Hotfix for a discovered measurement bug (streaming first-byte timestamp skew) that affected early Q1 baseline numbers; includes backfill notes.
Thread discussing final TTFT/TPOT definitions for streaming vs non-streaming APIs; includes debate on client vs server timing and proposal for ADR wording.
Thread coordinating a benchmark run that showed high variance; participants share runner logs, GPU clock settings, and suspected noisy-neighbor causes.
Thread reviewing a scheduler fairness tweak; links to GitHub PR and early before/after numbers; requests additional traffic shapes.
Thread about workload suite versioning and how to handle changing ‘top models’ during the quarter without invalidating comparisons.
Thread triaging a perf-canary failure on a release branch; includes rerun requests, suspected telemetry skew, and decision to block merge pending fix.
Thread between SRE and Runtime on what constitutes a ‘release blocker’ regression (thresholds, confidence, and exception criteria).
Thread about reserving GPU capacity for baseline runs; includes scheduling conflicts with other jobs and proposed quota/priority changes.
Thread reviewing the ADR draft for baseline metric definitions; includes comments about trace span naming and long-term compatibility.
Thread coordinating how baseline gates integrate into the runtime release checklist; includes rollout plan and who can approve exceptions.
Thread for a minor internal incident where baseline gate blocked multiple PRs due to a measurement bug; includes mitigation and follow-up action items.
Thread aligning telemetry pipeline requirements: artifact schemas, dashboard filters (model/SKU/region), and retention needed for quarter-over-quarter comparison.
Working spreadsheet-style doc tracking baseline runs by model/SKU/region, including run ids, variance notes, and links to artifacts/dashboards.
Informal notes consolidating candidate production traffic patterns, approximations used, and open questions for Applied ML/Evals about representativeness.
Draft proposal of gating thresholds (by workload), including suggested tolerance bands, rerun policy, and criteria for ‘expected’ seasonal variance.
Slides outline for exec readout: headline improvements/regressions vs prior quarter, biggest bottlenecks, and next quarter investment areas.
Experiment log doc comparing runner configurations (warmup length, affinity, clock pinning) and their impact on run-to-run variance.
Before/after analysis notes for scheduler changes (fairness/backpressure), including screenshots/links to dashboards and hypotheses for tail behavior.
Customer ticket reporting intermittent latency spikes; internal investigation references new instrumentation and baseline numbers to confirm no platform-wide regression.
Internal ticket requesting dedicated GPU reservation/time window for baseline runs; includes approvals, scheduling, and infra notes.
Support ticket about streaming TTFT discrepancies; resolved by clarifying measurement semantics and applying a runtime hotfix; links to related PR and Confluence ADR.
All-hands transcript segment where Runtime leadership summarizes the baseline initiative, why it matters, and what changes engineers will see in CI/release gating.
Technical deep dive transcript with a prospect focused on latency/throughput transparency; Redwood team references internal baselines and explains methodology at a high level.
Email thread between Runtime leadership and SRE/Telemetry stakeholders aligning on scope, resourcing, and timeline for Q1 baseline deliverables.
Executive sign-off thread for publishing the internal Q1 baseline report and enforcing baseline gates on release branches; includes risk/exception discussion.
CRM company record for an enterprise prospect with strict p95 latency requirements; notes reference performance deep dive and request for Redwood benchmark transparency.
CRM company record for a Dedicated/Private-leaning prospect with workload shape details and baseline expectations; links to a Fireflies technical deep dive meeting id.
